input.summary:
Front porch furnished in parts/room-4.mjs: a bench of two spruce stairs by the door, a barrel, axe-rack post and peg rail at the west end, a chopping stump and two barrels at the east end, all on the back row z=7, with the z=6 lane and x=13 step lane clear.
Two hanging lanterns on iron chains from the porch roof slab at (6,3,7) and (16,3,7) light the ends; with the fittings lanterns at (12,3,6) and (14,3,6) added, the room measures min light 11, 0 dark, and all 28 floor cells walk-reachable.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with 15 blocks from this part and no refused writes or off-palette blocks; `mcd room` says OK; the room render was read once.
left: The fittings lanterns at (12,3,6) and (14,3,6) are not in my copy (Fittings is a stub here); I verified with a temporary copy that they do not break the walk and raise min light to 11. The merged build should keep them.

I added two lanterns the elements.md list does not name: (6,3,7) and (16,3,7), each on an iron_chain at y=4 from the porch roof slab. The lamplighter or Fittings owner should know, so the lantern count in plan.md stays right.

The axe rack is a two-high spruce_fence post and the peg rail is a row of spruce_fence at y=3. Flower pots and item frames are not in the palette, so boots and axes are only suggested by the shapes, not shown as objects.
I did not tick any plan.md checklist item: the porch deck and posts belong to P1, the porch lanterns to P4, and no elements.md item is mine alone. plan.md Notes is unchanged.
The room render (room.png) is from above only; it was read once, and the furniture reads as a bench, barrels and posts, not as a finished interior at this scale.

waste.what: I worked out the front-porch cell layout by hand: which cells are lane, which are furniture, and which x/z each row character maps to, then built the layers() rows around them.
waste.cost: about 10 minutes of reasoning and 3 retries on the row strings and the lane/light placement
waste.tool: A `mcd plan` variant that prints the room's free cells with the lane and walk-required cells pre-marked (z=6 lane, x=13 gap) would let the furnisher draw the legend straight onto it.

waste.what: To test walking and light with the fittings lanterns, I wrote a throwaway script that loads build.nbt, adds the two lanterns and chains, and saves a test copy.
waste.cost: one script, one run, then deleted
waste.tool: `mcd room --with-planned <plan.md>` or a `--assume lanterns` flag that adds the plan's named fittings to the check, so the room check does not depend on another part being built.

waste.what: The light check ran on my copy without the fittings lanterns, so min light read 8 instead of the 11 the merged build will have.
waste.tool: The same `--with-planned` flag, or `mcd light` taking plan-named lamp positions.

companions.task: Build the axe rack and the peg rail (fence posts at head height against the back wall) so they read as joinery, and cut the bench seats to fit the wall.
Make the barrels and the chopping stump sit square at the east and west ends and check the barrel facings.
